messages:
zoe: hey team - bit of a messy tax situation. I was contracting through a US vendor and paid as a 1099-NEC through June 2025 while living in Toronto. I converted to direct hire in Canada on 2025-07-01. I just received a 1099-NEC from the vendor for 2025 showing payments Jan-Jun, and my Canadian payroll portal shows a T4 for July-Dec. worried about duplicate reporting and CRA/IRS issues. any advice?

maria (People Ops): thanks for bringing this up, @zoe. high-level: vendor-issued 1099s reflect what the vendor reported to the IRS for payments they made to you. T4s reflect what our Canadian payroll reported to the CRA. they can both exist without being duplicates if they cover different payers/periods. but if the company also issued employee wages covering Jan-Jun as retro pay, that could create overlap. can you confirm the vendor invoice IDs and the payroll ticket?

zoe: vendor invoice IDs: USV-221, USV-233. payroll ticket: PAY-4890. paystub snippets attached to PAY-4890 show T4 earnings (post-conversion): "T4 box 14: CAD 28,000". the 1099 shows USD 14,500 for Jan-Jun. i'm a canadian resident for 2025. i'm worried about foreign tax credit, whether the 1099 triggers IRS filing, and potential withholding reconciliation.

kevin (Payroll): @zoe we pulled PAY-4890. initial check: company payroll did not post any retro wages for Jan-Jun 2025; the T4 reflects only July-Dec payroll. vendor clearly issued 1099-NEC to you for payments they made. so likely no duplicate payroll from our side. action: we'll still reconcile GL entries to confirm we didn't record contractor-to-employee retro pay accidentally. ETA: 48 hours.

lucy (Tax Counsel): tax note: as a Canadian resident you report worldwide income to the CRA. The 1099-NEC is an IRS form and indicates the vendor reported those US payments to the IRS. Even if you live in Canada, the vendor may have had US reporting obligations. Key points: 1) You may need to file a US return if the IRS has a record of the 1099, but nonresident filing rules apply; 2) On your Canadian return you report the USD income (convert to CAD) and can claim foreign tax credits for any US tax actually paid; 3) If the vendor erroneously issued a 1099 for amounts we paid and we also reported wages on a T4/W-2, we can request a corrected 1099.

zoe: ok good to know. so if payroll confirms we didn't pay Jan-Jun, then it's just vendor income and my Canadian return will include both vendor (converted CAD) and T4 wages. will payroll provide a letter showing what we reported to CRA/IRS? my accountant asked for documentation.

kevin (Payroll): yes we can provide a verification letter summarizing the payroll amounts we reported and that no retro wages for Jan-Jun were processed by Redwood. we'll attach it to PAY-4890. if we had posted retro wages we'd coordinate a vendor correction. payroll-bot: queueing GL reconciliation.

payroll-bot: PAY-4890 reconciliation started  assigned to kevin  expected completion: 48 hours. :gear:

lucy (Tax Counsel): additional note: if the vendor withheld any US tax (unlikely for 1099-NEC) or you made estimated payments, keep records. For CRA foreign tax credit, your accountant will need proof of foreign tax paid and the foreign income amounts. We can issue a payroll letter and a year-end summary.

zoe: thanks everyone. i'll upload the vendor remittance advices and the 1099 PDF to PAY-4890 now. appreciate the quick triage. :relieved:
